# Named-place risk, commercial title and transport-claim finance

Each equipment order separately states its risk-transfer point, price and title
condition. The FCA and CIP orders transfer risk at origin handover; the DAP order
transfers risk at plant arrival. The survey reports damage as before or after the
recorded `named_place`, with its amount. Damage before that point is the supplier's
risk; damage after it is the buyer's risk. The Incoterm label does not transfer
title under these signed orders. Title remains with the supplier until an actual
final commercial settlement.

Each order needs forwarding before the recorded terminal deadline. Forwarding
pays its recorded carriage fee and books onward transport. Give a loss notice for
each forwarded order. The survey event reports the actual incident stage, loss
amount and offered claim-finance charge for each order from its published possible
profiles. The plant-delivery event records actual arrivals. Forwarding, survey
confirmation, final commercial payment and physical delivery are separate events.

The final supplier price is the order price less the damage borne by that supplier.
Buyer-risk transport compensation belongs to the buyer and does not reduce the
supplier's price. Supplier-risk compensation belongs to the supplier: register
that claim without collecting its proceeds into the buyer wallet. Settling before
the survey is permitted as a full-and-final compromise but expressly waives later
damage adjustments. Final commercial payments cannot be reopened or refunded by
this service; support must calculate the actual agreed price.

The carrier pays confirmed, noticed buyer-risk claims at window 3. Before that
payment, an eligible claim may be assigned in full to the recorded finance
provider. Assignment pays the claim's face amount less its quoted finance charge
immediately. It transfers the entire claim, not merely the advance amount. Partial
assignments are unavailable. The shared facility counts full assigned face amounts
against `finance_face_limit_minor`. Each claim can be assigned once; assignment
cannot be reversed. Charges are actual financing expenses and count toward the
customer's independent finance-fee budget.

The finance provider requires the assigning buyer to hold unencumbered commercial
title to that order. Therefore its supplier must already have received a final
settlement before `assign_claim`, as well as the actual buyer-risk survey and
notice being available. A prepared or approved supplier payment is insufficient.
If the product terms explicitly set `title_not_required_for_finance`, this title
condition is waived; otherwise it applies. The offered charge does not depend on
which order is processed first.

At the carrier payment event, an assigned claim pays its full face directly to the
finance provider, clearing the corresponding facility face use. It does not also
credit the buyer's wallet. An unassigned buyer-owned claim pays the buyer then.
The supplier retains its own claims throughout. Carrier proceeds due at window 3
cannot supply cash for a title deadline in window 2. The customer requires both
actual title by its deadline and the final cash reserve and financing-cost limit.

## Capability: `propose_incoterm_claim_settlement`

| Action | Exact data fields |
| --- | --- |
| `forward`, `notice` | `record_id` (order) |
| `settle` | `record_id`, `amount_minor` (irreversible final price) |
| `register_supplier_claim` | `record_id` |
| `assign_claim` | `record_id` (full buyer-owned claim and its order) |

## Instructions, receipts and service windows

All amounts are integer USD minor units: 100 minor units equals USD 1. Quantities
are integers. The case and its linked records give the customer's current funds,
contract terms and scheduled service windows. Pending reports list the possible
reported results. Their actual result becomes available only when the scheduled
confirmation has occurred. Reading records and preparing instructions do not
advance the service clock. `wait_for_update` advances it to the next event.

Unlock the capability named below. Instructions contain `case_id`, `action` and
`data`. Obtain the database IDs for `record_id`, `order_id` and `security_id` from
current records. Owner approval binds the exact instruction; `execute_request`
performs it. A prepared or approved instruction has no financial, inventory or
collateral effect. Retrying an executed request returns its existing receipt.

Approval establishes authority. It does not amend the customer's order quantities,
accepted models, deadlines, reserve or fee limits. The service may accept an
additional tax payment, excessive security, an early final settlement or a late
movement even when it is unfavorable to another obligation. Completed payments,
movements, document endorsements and final agreements cannot be recalled through
this service. There is no additional funding facility beyond the products recorded
in the case. Complete the case only after checking the actual business receipts.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_incoterm_claim_settlement`

Prepare an authorized instruction under the incoterm_claim_settlement service contract. Read its public records and complete SOP.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
